parameter: P(Woocalla reduced facies present at the top of the Pandurra)
in_state_source_and_date: RB 72/00189 pp. 15-18 (1971 LD holes, statement 33); PMR 58/74 (statements 13, 19); mesac31775 (statement 12)
evidence_and_translation: Six of the seven 1971 LD holes between Oakden Hills and Lake Dutton cut Woocalla black or dolomitic shale (12 to 129 m); six of six Noranda holes 10 km apart; the black-shale facies fills broad basins around the Pandurra ridges and is traced to Woomera No. 1 (308 to 454 m), inside the window. Translated as a window share well above Annex A's 0.05 to 0.30, because this facies is known in the window, with the upper bound held below the corridor's 6 of 7 since the facies is absent at Yudnapinna and LD7

parameter: Woocalla basin geometry: belt length; aspect; strike; depression coupling
proposed_distribution: Belt length LogUniform(30, 150) km; aspect 3.2 (fixed); strike north-south, 10 deg (fixed); depression weight 1 over a 20 km running mean (fixed)
evidence_and_translation: Mineralised black shale in a basement trough 32 km long, corridor 10 km wide trending slightly east of north (the Annex A fabric); the controlling disconformity traced 145 km to the Pandurra prospect; the facies fills broad basins and the 1968 Winnie Pinnie troughs are 1.6 to 3.2 by 0.8 km. The field is the Annex A anisotropic field with an added depression term: the top of the Pandurra below its 20 km running mean, weighted equally (declared; Maiden gives 'associated with depressions', no number)

parameter: Favourable zone: distance from the reduced facies edge (shoreline) within which copper bodies form
proposed_distribution: Reach LogUniform(1, 15) km inside the reduced facies from its edge
evidence_and_translation: Cu highest near the basin edge and falling over 15 km (4,600 ppm at 1 km to 180 ppm at 15 km); north of the Cattlegrid 5,700 to 6,500 ppm at 0.25 to 0.75 km from the palaeo-shoreline, 2,400 ppm at 1.25 km; copper inshore, Pb-Zn offshore; a rapid oxidising-to-reducing change as a control. The Mount Gunson margin is the facies edge, as the basalt edge is Annex A's

parameter: Copper body intensity in the favourable zone
proposed_distribution: LogUniform(50, 300) per 10^4 km2 of favourable zone
evidence_and_translation: The Mount Gunson field: Gunyah, Sweet Nell, East Lagoon, Cattle Grid, the Gully and the Pb-Zn zones, about five copper bodies in a corridor of roughly 32 by 10 km of which perhaps a third is favourable: of order 150 per 10^4 km2 of favourable ground. Declared from that count; the window's zone area then sets the number
